question:
A function is defined by $h(x)=\sec^{-1}\left(\dfrac{3}{x-1}\right)$.

(a) Determine the domain of $h$.

(b) Determine its range.

(c) Find all values of $x$ for which $h(x)=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ or $h(x)=\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$.
explanation:
(a)
The expression is defined only when $x\neq1$. Also, the argument of $\sec^{-1}$ must satisfy
$$\left|\frac{3}{x-1}\right|\geq1$$
Therefore,
$$0<|x-1|\leq3$$
This gives
$$-3\leq x-1<0\quad\text{or}\quad0Hence,
$$-2\leq x<1\quad\text{or}\quad1Therefore, the domain is
$$[-2,1)\cup(1,4]$$

(b)
On the domain, the argument $\dfrac{3}{x-1}$ assumes all values satisfying $|t|\geq1$. Therefore, the range is the principal-value range of $\sec^{-1}t$:
$$\left[0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\cup\left(\frac{\pi}{2},\pi\right]$$

(c)
For $h(x)=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$,
$$\frac{3}{x-1}=\sec\frac{\pi}{3}=2$$
Therefore,
$$2x-2=3$$
$$x=\frac{5}{2}$$
For $h(x)=\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$,
$$\frac{3}{x-1}=\sec\frac{3\pi}{4}=-\sqrt{2}$$
Therefore,
$$x-1=-\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}$$
$$x=1-\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}$$
Both values belong to the domain. Hence, the required values are
$$x=\frac{5}{2}\quad\text{and}\quad x=1-\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}$$
